name: nginx -t
description: Test the configuration files for syntax errors without (re)starting nginx.

examples.description: Check the config and report the file and line of any error
examples.output:
nginx: the configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf syntax is ok
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test is successful

examples.command: sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
examples.description: Only reload if the config is valid
Test an alternative config file

notes: Always run nginx -t before reloading; a broken config makes restart fail and takes the site down.
Use sudo so nginx can read certificates and write its pid/log files during the test.

name: nginx -T
description: Test the configuration and print the full, merged config including all included files.

examples.description: Print every loaded config file
Find which server blocks define which hostnames
Page through the effective configuration

notes: Great for debugging which include actually contains a directive. Output can contain sensitive values, so don't paste it publicly.

name: nginx -v
description: Show the nginx version, or -V for build options and compiled-in modules.

examples.description: Print the version
List compiled-in modules
Find the default config file path

notes: nginx prints version info to stderr, so redirect 2>&1 before piping.

name: nginx -c
description: Start nginx using a specific configuration file.

flags.description: Set the prefix path for relative paths
Set global directives from the command line

examples.description: Start with an explicit config path
Run from a project directory with a local prefix (useful for dev/testing)
Run in the foreground (common in Docker containers)

name: nginx -s reload
description: Gracefully reload the configuration without dropping connections.

examples.description: Start new workers with the new config; old workers finish their requests
Same via systemd (preferred on systemd hosts)

notes: If the new config is invalid, nginx keeps running with the old config and logs the error. Run nginx -t first to see the problem.

name: nginx -s
description: Send a stop, quit or reopen signal to the running nginx master process.

examples.description: Graceful shutdown: wait for workers to finish current requests
Fast shutdown: terminate immediately
Reopen log files (used after log rotation)

notes: stop drops in-flight requests; prefer quit in production.

name: systemctl nginx
description: Manage the nginx service with systemd.

examples.description: Check whether nginx is running and see recent log lines
Reload config gracefully
Full stop and start (e.g. after upgrading the nginx package)
Start now and on every boot
Stop the service
Restart nginx installed with Homebrew on macOS

notes: Prefer reload over restart: restart briefly drops all connections.
If you start nginx manually with the nginx binary, systemd won't know about it; stick to one method.

name: ln -s sites-available sites-enabled
description: Enable or disable a site using the Debian/Ubuntu sites-available/sites-enabled layout.

examples.description: Create the site's server block
Enable the site
Disable the default site (removes only the symlink)

examples.command: sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
examples.description: Validate and apply

notes: Use an absolute path for the symlink source; relative targets break silently.
RHEL/Fedora and the official nginx.org packages use /etc/nginx/conf.d/*.conf instead; just add or remove .conf files there.

name: tail access.log
description: Follow and analyze the access log.

examples.description: Stream requests as they arrive
Count responses by status code (default combined format)

examples.command: sudo awk '{print $1}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
examples.description: Top client IPs

notes: The awk column numbers assume the default "combined" log_format.

name: tail error.log
description: Follow the error log to debug failed requests, upstream errors and config problems.

examples.description: Stream errors as they happen
Find recent upstream/proxy errors (e.g. 502s)
Follow startup/shutdown messages from systemd

notes: Raise verbosity temporarily with error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log debug; (requires a build with --with-debug) or info/notice.

name: server { }
description: Define a virtual host that serves static files for a domain.

examples.description: Basic static site on port 80
SPA fallback: serve index.html for client-side routes

notes: Place in /etc/nginx/sites-available/<site> or /etc/nginx/conf.d/<site>.conf.
The first server block for a port (or the one marked default_server) handles requests with no matching server_name.

name: proxy_pass
description: Forward requests to a backend application such as Node, Python or Go.

examples.description: Proxy all requests to an app on port 3000 with standard forwarded headers
Trailing slash on proxy_pass strips the /api/ prefix before forwarding
Load balance across several backends (round robin)

notes: proxy_pass with a URI (e.g. trailing /) replaces the matched location prefix; without one the original path is passed unchanged.
502 Bad Gateway usually means the backend is down or the address/port is wrong; check the error log.

name: proxy_set_header Upgrade
description: Proxy WebSocket connections to a backend.

examples.description: Pass WebSocket upgrade headers and keep idle connections open for an hour

notes: Without proxy_http_version 1.1 and the Upgrade/Connection headers, WebSocket handshakes fail.

name: return 301
description: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS or one domain to another.

examples.description: Redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS
Redirect www to the apex domain
Redirect a single path

notes: Prefer return over rewrite for simple redirects; it is faster and clearer.
Use 302 while testing; browsers cache 301 aggressively.

name: listen 443 ssl
description: Serve a site over HTTPS with TLS certificates.

examples.description: HTTPS server with HTTP/2 and HSTS
Obtain a Let's Encrypt certificate and configure nginx automatically

notes: The standalone http2 directive requires nginx 1.25.1+; older versions use listen 443 ssl http2;.
Use fullchain.pem, not cert.pem, or some clients will fail to verify the chain.

name: client_max_body_size
description: Raise the maximum allowed request body size (fixes 413 Request Entity Too Large).

examples.description: Allow uploads up to 50 MB (in http, server or location)
Disable the size check for one location

notes: The default is 1M.
Your backend (PHP upload_max_filesize, app framework limits) may also need raising.

name: gzip on
description: Enable gzip compression for text-based responses.

examples.description: Typical gzip settings for the http block

notes: text/html is always compressed when gzip is on; don't list it in gzip_types (it triggers a duplicate warning).
Don't gzip already-compressed formats like JPEG, PNG or ZIP.

name: expires
description: Set long cache headers for static assets.

examples.description: Cache static assets for 30 days and skip access logging
Immutable caching for fingerprinted build assets

notes: Only use long or immutable caching for files with content hashes in their names.
add_header in a location replaces all add_header directives inherited from the server block.

name: fastcgi_pass
description: Pass PHP requests to PHP-FPM (e.g. Laravel or WordPress).

examples.description: Laravel-style front controller with PHP-FPM over a Unix socket (Debian/Ubuntu)

notes: The socket path depends on your PHP version and distro; check ls /run/php/.
snippets/fastcgi-php.conf ships with Debian/Ubuntu; elsewhere use include fastcgi_params; and set SCRIPT_FILENAME yourself.

name: auth_basic
description: Password-protect a location with HTTP basic authentication.

examples.description: Create the password file with user admin (htpasswd is in apache2-utils / httpd-tools)
Require a login for /admin

notes: htpasswd -c overwrites an existing file; omit -c when adding more users.
Only use basic auth over HTTPS; credentials are sent base64-encoded, not encrypted.

name: limit_req
description: Rate-limit requests per client IP to protect login pages and APIs.

examples.description: Allow 10 req/s per IP with a burst of 20, returning 429 when exceeded

notes: limit_req_zone must be declared in the http context; limit_req goes in server or location.
Behind a load balancer, $binary_remote_addr is the balancer's IP unless you configure the realip module.
